stem: An urban planning study measures the commute time (minutes) for a sample of 20 city workers. The sample mean is 33.0 min with a sample standard deviation of 6.9 min. However, 2 of the 20 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 18 observations have a mean of 30.9 min and standard deviation of 5.1 min. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 33.0, 95% CI = [29.8, 36.2]. Without outliers: mean = 30.9, 95% CI = [28.5, 33.3]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [28.5, 36.2]. Point estimate: 31.9 min.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [28.5, 36.2].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
